Hearing before the New York City Council’s Committee on Health Intro. 1B : Designating the Animal Care Centers of NYC facility in the borough of Queens, as the Paul A. Vallone Queens Animal Care Center.

March 7, 2024

Good morning. I am Michelle Villagomez, New York City Legislative Senior Director for the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ASPCA). I would like to thank Health Committee Chair Schulman, and Speaker Adams for this opportunity. I am honored to provide testimony in support of the proposed legislation to rename the Queens Animal Care Center after the late Councilmember Paul Vallone. He was a wonderful ally in the work of the ASPCA, and I genuinely enjoyed collaborating with him. As a resident of Queens and his district, I believe this renaming would be a fitting tribute to a man who dedicated himself to the well-being of both animals and the community he served. Councilmember Paul Vallone's commitment to animal welfare was not only a personal passion but also a continuation of his family's legacy. The Vallone family has long been synonymous with advocating for the welfare of animals in New York City. Councilmember Vallone's father, Speaker Peter Vallone, played a pivotal role in passing legislation in 2000 that mandated the establishment of five full-service animal shelters across the city. His mother, Tina Vallone, demonstrated unwavering dedication as a volunteer in various animal welfare initiatives throughout the years, and his brother Councilmember Peter Vallone was a staunch advocate against animal cruelty. Paul Vallone carried this torch forward with great fervor. In 2018, he championed legislation to ensure that all five boroughs have access to full-service animal shelters. He recognized that animal shelters are not merely facilities for housing stray pets but vital community resources offering a wide array of services, including surrender prevention, food assistance, medical care, humane education, and adoption programs. He understood that by supporting animal welfare, we also support the well-being of our communities. His vision for the Queens

Animal Care Center was one of inclusivity and compassion, where both animals and people could find the assistance and resources they needed. Renaming the center in his honor would not only commemorate his dedication and hard work but also serve as a reminder of the profound connection between human and animal welfare. The Queens Animal Care Center, under its new name, will serve as a lasting reminder of Paul Vallone's legacy of empathy, kindness, and commitment to making our world a better place for all living beings. In conclusion, I urge the Health Committee and the City Council to support this important initiative, ensuring that Paul Vallone's legacy continues to inspire and uplift us all. It is imperative that we continue to invest in and advance the services provided by animal care centers throughout New York City. By doing so, we honor his memory and ensure that his compassionate spirit lives on. Thank you.
